task: Office support compose SQL migration filename provenance alignment with actual installed Fresh Install ledger

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This work is critical migration provenance, not a feature change. A false second migration version could replay privileged role grants, so the exact hosted ledger version, immutable SQL source bytes, deletion of obsolete alias, and dependent tests require proof; source checks do not establish authenticated provider runtime.

acceptanceCriteria: Only the source filename changes from the uninstalled future timestamp 20261019090000 to the installed 20261019073857 timestamp, SQL bytes unchanged.
Both migration-dependent Vitest source paths are updated and run without accessing a hosted database.
Original forward composer foundation and canonical explicit owner denial continue to pass all tests.
No hosted SQL write, browser feature rollout or other tenant account is changed during parity adjustment.
invariants: The Fresh Install migration ledger retains its actual version 20261019073857 and name office_support_compose_default_v1.
The SQL body remains exactly the code already executed on Fresh Install under the same correction name.
Owner explicit deny precedes inherited support grant; only support inherits office.email.compose.
No duplicate future-named SQL migration remains in source code after correction.
forbiddenStates: Creating an invented 20261019090000 migration ledger record to silence source reconciliation.
Reapplying the already installed support capability migration while renaming source.
Replacing a verified SQL role grant with a broader grant or updated body.
Accidentally enabling mail send or restoring the paused staging project.

failureModes: Git migration runner considers differently named SQL to be an unapplied new migration and replays it.
Source alias is left in repository while the corrected filename is added, producing duplicate logical migration.
Test fixtures still load the removed filename and fail after source relocation.
The rename subtly alters SQL body whitespace or conditional authorization semantics.
Source proof reports database runtime acceptance without a signed session or enabled mailbox.
edgeCases: The installed migration's timestamp precedes the original proposed file timestamp by roughly twenty-one minutes.
A merge of this branch while #1443 is stacked must preserve that exact child's source path references.
No existing file may occupy the corrected timestamp and migration name.
The same installed correction must appear as one mapping, not two independently runnable SQL entries.
The change must not generate a new Supabase apply_migration call even during CI.

alternatives.summary: Rename the same forward-only SQL bytes to the exact already installed migration ledger version.
alternatives.reason: Preserves the canonical database truth and eliminates duplicate migration replay while retaining unchanged source content.

alternatives.summary: Insert a second migration ledger row with the original future filename without running its SQL.
alternatives.reason: Fabricates a historical migration event that did not occur and violates the immutable provenance principle.

alternatives.summary: Keep both filename versions in repository and rely on idempotent role grant on future installs.
alternatives.reason: Creates duplicate executable source identities and obscures which version was actually applied.

specialistReviews.finding: The managed ledger version and source filename disagree even though the SQL payload is applied.
specialistReviews.resolution: Rename to the actually installed version, check same SQL blob SHA, and reject duplicate future source.

specialistReviews.finding: Replaying even an idempotent role grant at a second version could normalize away an intended owner restriction in future edits.
specialistReviews.resolution: Retain identical single SQL body, no personal overrides and fail-closed context before source parity is claimed.

specialistReviews.finding: Static string references to the obsolete filename could make the corrected path look missing or suppress a test.
specialistReviews.resolution: Update both exact Vitest source paths and verify no remaining executable alias in this release branch.

specialistReviews.finding: A source rename might be confused with authorization to deploy Office UI or rerun the managed migration.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep hosted writes and Vercel preview blocked until independent proof and the correct staging-isolated environment.

challenge.scenario: Supabase migration runner scans source filenames after already recording 20261019073857.
challenge.finding: The old future-timestamp SQL appears unapplied and could be executed twice.
challenge.resolution: Keep only filename matching the actual logged version.

challenge.scenario: A developer copies SQL rather than moving the same Git blob.
challenge.finding: Both source names survive, creating duplicate migration candidates.
challenge.resolution: Delete original path and add corrected path with byte-identical content.

challenge.scenario: A source-identity checker hashes bytes after the rename.
challenge.finding: A changed SQL whitespace byte could silently affect canonical provenance.
challenge.resolution: Compare exact source contents and preserve its Git blob identity.

challenge.scenario: An existing test reads the earlier 20261019090000 path.
challenge.finding: Read fails despite the correct SQL existing in the new location.
challenge.resolution: Update both impacted Vitest paths and rerun tests.

challenge.scenario: Owner previously denied an individual support employee composing email.
challenge.finding: A poorly implemented replay could replace the denial with a grant.
challenge.resolution: Preserve only role preset upsert with no user overrides or new grant semantics.

challenge.scenario: An Alap tenant tries to use the advanced Digital Office after migration mapping.
challenge.finding: Source movement cannot authorize a Pro workspace under Alap.
challenge.resolution: No subscription or server entitlement function modification.

challenge.scenario: Preview Vercel build points at paused staging rather than Fresh Install.
challenge.finding: UI testing on that preview risks false failure and wrong datastore writes.
challenge.resolution: Keep all preview deployments disabled until correct isolated environment is proven.

challenge.scenario: The installed ledger already has the correction and no mailbox configured.
challenge.finding: Marking source parity as full send acceptance creates a false readiness claim.
challenge.resolution: Restrict success wording to the exact source-to-ledger identity and no hosted runtime write.

proofPlan: Check the exact installed Fresh Install schema_migrations version and name using read-only Supabase query.
Keep original SQL Git blob content unmodified and rename only its source path, with current branch as change base.
Verify both migration-dependent tests and full source security, TypeScript and build CI on the exact new source SHA.
Require Completion Truth and explicit lifecycle closure without claiming managed JWT or Vercel preview readiness.
operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The managed Fresh Install ledger contains the already applied support compose SQL at version 20261019073857 but the unmerged repository calls the byte-identical migration 20261019090000, which would create false replay risk for future schema tooling.
observableOutcomes: Canonical repository SQL filename equals the existing hosted migration ledger version and migration name without rewriting any SQL bytes.
Original later filename is removed so automated source migration reconciliation cannot treat the already applied capability correction as a second migration.
Tests retain role-only compose, explicit deny priority and mailbox fail-closed authority while mapping to exact source file.
unresolvedRisks: Vercel preview branch still inherits inactive staging URL and must not be used until isolated Fresh credentials are resolved.
Changing a source filename cannot attest full hosted signed JWT end-user draft-save semantics.
Other historical Office source migration ordering remains separately governed by the installed six prior Fresh rows and existing integration PR.

in: Rename one not-yet-main forward SQL migration filename to actual installed ledger version, preserving file bytes.
Correct exact path references in two targeted static regressions and update existing PO receipt.
out: Never invoke apply_migration or mutate Supabase migration ledger again.
No production Vercel deployment, secret copying, platform/staging project state change or Office mailbox creation.
No source SQL body rewrite or change of accepted support inheritance semantics.

requirements.requirement: Repository source migration filename exactly matches already installed Fresh Install ledger timestamp while preserving SQL body bytes and role grant.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No duplicate future-named SQL migration, fabricated ledger history, tenant mutation or mailbox activation is allowed.

notes: New bounded provenance transaction after prior #1442 source-only VERIFIED_DONE / CLOSED. Fresh Install applied office_support_compose_default_v1 with actual ledger version 20261019073857, not source file initial future filename 20261019090000. Rename the source file with BYTE-IDENTICAL content and retarget two tests. No hosted DB write, no fake migration history, no mailbox activation.
